steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Supply-side policies aim to increase the economy's productive capacity by improving the efficiency and quality of factors of production.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Investment in education and training: improves human capital, increases productivity, reduces structural unemployment by giving workers transferable skills.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Lower direct taxes and business taxes: increase incentives to work and invest, but may reduce government revenue.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Privatisation and deregulation: introduces competition and profit incentives, improving efficiency — but natural monopolies may exploit consumers.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain how investment in education and training can improve the UK's economic performance. | Describe the potential advantages and disadvantages of privatisation. | Evaluate whether supply-side policies are more effective than demand-side policies for long-term economic growth.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Supply-side policies affect PRODUCTION (capacity), demand-side policies affect DEMAND (spending). Always give SPECIFIC examples: education, lower taxes, privatisation, deregulation. Supply-side improvements take a LONG TIME but have PERMANENT effects.
